 Ram Rati

Coram:
Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal

Order
% 15.12.2023 CM APPL. 64968/2023 (for delay in filing)
1. This is an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act. 1963 seeking condonation of delay in filing the present appeal.
2. For the reasons stated in the application, the delay of 38 days in filing the present appeal is condoned.
3. The application stands disposed of.

1. This is an appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 impugning the judgment dated 01.08.2023 passed by the Additional District Judge, Rohini, New Delhi ('Reference Court') in LAC No. 30/2020 seeking further enhancement of the compensation amount in respect of award No. 12/2005-06 pertaining to the land acquired of Village Barwala, Delhi.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Rohini, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/12/2023 at 22:07:12 2.
The following relief has been sought by the appellant:

"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed to YOUR LORDSHIPS that the appeal may kindly be accepted and the market value of the land of the appellant be further enhanced by Rs. 50,000/ per bigha besides other statutory benefits as admissible under Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended up to date, be passed in favour of the Ram Rati vs Union Of India & Anr on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113561060/
1 Appellant and against the respondents and the appellant be further granted additional amount as provided under section 23 (I A) and Solatium as provided under section 23(2) and interest on the said sums as per the judgment of Sunder's case be modifying the order judgment & order dated 01-08-2023, passed by the Learned lower court of Sh. Deepak Dabas, ADJ, Rohini, Delhi in the case bearing LAC No. 30/2020 titled as "Ram Rati Versus Union of lndia & Anr."
Cost of the appeal be also awarded in favour of the humble Appellant.
